title: keyMaterial client: read partialSuccess with no successful client as 'no usable key material', not a decode error
description:
Decision proposed 2026-11-14 (Mark agreed): keep the codec strict, add a narrow leniency on the keyMaterial client path. Today Haven's every-client-exhausted answer (userStatus=partialSuccess, one client with keyMaterialExhausted, no success; Haven DIV-13; vector km-09; seen live for grace on mimi.havenmessenger.com) fails in mimid as DecodingError 'clients list does not match userStatus PartialSuccess', so the user sees an error instead of 'no keys available, try later'.

Change: where mimid consumes a KeyMaterialResponse as a requester (PeerClient callers, mimid-chat /invite, the follower path), a partialSuccess whose clients are all keyMaterialExhausted or nothingCompatible is treated like noCompatibleMaterial, i.e. no usable key material. Log it as a peer divergence (warn, with the peer domain). The wire decoder stays strict on its own, so either add a lenient decode entry point used only by the client path or a typed 'divergent but understood' result; don't loosen KeyMaterialResponse::tls_deserialize for everyone. Hub-side (when mimid answers keyMaterial) is unchanged.

Tests: the Haven fixture key_material_response_exhausted.bin and vector km-09 map to 'no usable key material'. A partialSuccess with zero clients, or with a client in success status but no KeyPackage, is still refused.

Related spec gap (no userStatus for 'every client exhausted'): IETF-qxjl. Supersedes the 'refuse' half of decision mimid-1wgh.5.63 for the client path only.
